title: How Underground Mining Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain underground mining: how it differs from surface and mountaintop removal mining, the history from ancient Egyptian, Roman and prehistoric mining (fire setting, pick axes, slave and prisoner labor) through mechanization, and the basic shaft layout of mines. They cover hard rock versus soft rock mines, and the methods room and pillar (continuous miner), cut and fill, block caving, long wall and short wall mining. They discuss mining dangers and health risks (black lung, collapses, explosions, gases), the 2010 Chilean mine rescue, 2010 disasters in West Virginia and New Zealand, environmental damage including the Centralia mine fire and wildcat gold mining in Guiana, and the canary in a coal mine, John Scott Haldane's carbon monoxide experiments, and birds' respiratory systems. The episode closes with a listener mail about a Seattle pirate radio station.

segments.title: Opening banter and Chilean mine rescue
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce underground mining, contrast it with mountaintop removal and fracking, and discuss the 2010 Chilean mine rescue and the number of miners who die on the job.

segments.title: Black lung and surface versus underground mining
segments.summary: The hosts discuss black lung, its preventability, and how surface mining differs from underground mining, including the depth at which each becomes efficient.

segments.title: History of mining from ancient times
segments.summary: Early mining from prehistoric and Egyptian and Roman times used pick axes and prisoner or slave labor. Fire setting was used to crack rock. Mining evolved as tools moved from flint and bone to copper, bronze and iron.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Break before the discussion of mechanized mining techniques.

segments.title: Mine anatomy and hard rock versus soft rock
segments.summary: Mines have ventilation, access, exit and recovery shafts, and the ore deposit determines the mining technique. The hosts debate whether hard or soft refers to the ore or the surrounding rock; examples of hard rock and soft rock ores are listed.

segments.title: Room and pillar, cut and fill, and block caving
segments.summary: Room and pillar mining uses a continuous miner to carve rooms and leave pillars for support. Cut and fill backfills each cut with rubble for vertical deposits. Block caving lets the roof collapse and is used for low grade ore.

segments.title: Long wall and short wall mining
segments.summary: Long wall mining uses a large shearer machine that cuts coal onto a conveyor while hydraulic supports hold up the roof, and short wall mining is a similar method for narrower deposits. The hosts express enthusiasm for these machines.

segments.title: John Henry and tunneling
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether John Henry's railroad tunnel work counts as mining, and recall past civil engineering episodes on tunnels and bridges.

segments.title: Environmental damage, Centralia fire, and wildcat mining
segments.summary: Mining damages the environment through air and water pollution. The Centralia, Pennsylvania underground coal fire is described, along with illegal wildcat gold mining in Guiana that uses mercury.

segments.title: Mining disasters, health risks, and the canary
segments.summary: The hosts list major 2010 disasters and mention explosions, gas, and respiratory disease. They then describe John Scott Haldane's carbon monoxide experiments, the canary in a coal mine, and how birds' respiratory systems make them sensitive to bad air.
